item.title: Explain Echoes From Scratch

turns.text: Make a 10-second vertical explainer with voice-over about why we hear echoes. Write the words yourself, keep it easy for kids, and choose the look.

item.tests: Tests autonomous short-script writing and delivery of a complete narrated explainer rather than a script-only response.

answer_sheet.Topic and audience: Why we hear echoes, explained simply for kids.

must_haves: One approximately 10-second vertical video includes intelligible English voice-over.
The narration explains that sound reflects off a surface and returns to the listener.
The visuals show sound traveling from a source to a surface and back toward the listener.
The explanation uses simple, child-friendly language and finishes without cutting off the narration.
The visual sound journey and the spoken explanation agree.

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

style.prompt: Create a clear, scientifically accurate 5-second educational animated explainer titled 'Why We Hear Echoes'. Clean colorful 2D side-view diagram: a person on the left facing a distant stone cliff on the right, with a large open gap. Fixed camera. First, the person calls 'Hey!' and a visible stylized sound-wave pulse travels from the person toward the cliff. The pulse reflects off the cliff and returns to the person's ear, followed by a quieter repeated 'Hey!' illustrating the delay. Wave arcs are a diagrammatic representation of sound traveling through air, not objects. Show a simple outbound arrow labeled 'Sound' and a return arrow labeled 'Echo'. Friendly clear narrator says exactly: 'An echo is sound bouncing off a distant surface and returning to you.' Keep narration intelligible and prioritize it over the illustrative calls. Bright, uncluttered educational composition with readable labels; finish on the reflected wave reaching the listener. No music.
